A line plot displays the trend of a continuous variable over an ordered axis such as time. In biomedical research, line plots are the standard figure for growth curves, pharmacokinetic profiles, and longitudinal omics time courses, usually with an uncertainty band around the group mean. `CairoMakie` composes them from `lines!`, `band!`, and `scatter!` primitives with exact control over layering.

## Example

![](../images/Julia/LinePlot_demo.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

## Setup

- System Requirements: Cross-platform (Linux/MacOS/Windows)
- Programming Language: **Julia**
- Dependencies: `CairoMakie`, `DataFrames`, `Statistics`

```{julia}
#| label: packages-setup
#| output: false
using CairoMakie
using DataFrames
using Statistics
using Random
```

## Data Preparation

We simulate a preclinical tumor-growth study: 12 mice per arm (vehicle vs treatment) measured weekly for 8 weeks, using a two-phase exponential growth model with mouse-to-mouse variability.

```{julia}
#| label: data-prep
Random.seed!(21)

weeks = 0.0:8
n_mice = 12
arms = Dict("Vehicle" => 0.32, "Treatment" => 0.18)
curves = Dict{String, Matrix{Float64}}()
for (arm, rate) in arms
    curves[arm] = [100 * exp(rate * (1 + 0.08 * randn()) * w) for m in 1:n_mice, w in weeks]
end
arm_colors = Dict("Vehicle" => :steelblue, "Treatment" => :tomato)
```

## Visualization

### Basic Line Plot

Aggregate first, then draw: one line per group with distinct markers keeps small summaries readable.

```{julia}
#| label: fig-jl-line-basic
#| fig-cap: "Mean tumor size per week for the two treatment arms"
#| width: 480
fig = Figure(size = (460, 340))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1], xlabel = "Week", ylabel = "Tumor volume (mm\$^3\$)")
for (arm, mat) in curves
    lines!(ax, weeks, vec(mean(mat, dims = 1)); color = arm_colors[arm],
           linewidth = 2)
    scatter!(ax, weeks, vec(mean(mat, dims = 1)); color = arm_colors[arm],
             markersize = 10, marker = arm == "Vehicle" ? :circle : :rect)
end
hidespines!(ax, :t, :r)
Legend(fig[1, 2], [LineElement(color = :steelblue, linewidth = 2),
                   LineElement(color = :tomato, linewidth = 2)],
       ["Vehicle", "Treatment"], framevisible = false)
fig
```

### Line Plot with Confidence Band

A band between the mean ± 1.96 × SEM communicates sampling uncertainty; build it with `band!` behind the mean line.

```{julia}
#| label: fig-jl-line-ci
#| fig-cap: "Group mean with a ± 1.96 SEM band"
#| width: 480
fig = Figure(size = (460, 340))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1], xlabel = "Week", ylabel = "Tumor volume (mm\$^3\$)")
for (arm, mat) in curves
    m = vec(mean(mat, dims = 1))
    sem = vec(std(mat, dims = 1)) ./ sqrt(n_mice)
    band!(ax, weeks, m .- 1.96 .* sem, m .+ 1.96 .* sem;
          color = (arm_colors[arm], 0.2))
    lines!(ax, weeks, m; color = arm_colors[arm], linewidth = 2)
end
hidespines!(ax, :t, :r)
Legend(fig[1, 2], [LineElement(color = :steelblue, linewidth = 2),
                   LineElement(color = :tomato, linewidth = 2)],
       ["Vehicle", "Treatment"], framevisible = false)
fig
```

### Spaghetti Plot with Population Mean

Showing every subject as a thin line behind the bold group mean communicates both the trend and the animal-to-animal variability.

```{julia}
#| label: fig-jl-line-spaghetti
#| fig-cap: "Individual growth curves (thin) with the group mean (bold)"
#| width: 480
fig = Figure(size = (460, 340))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1], xlabel = "Week", ylabel = "Tumor volume (mm\$^3\$)")
for (arm, mat) in curves
    for m in 1:n_mice
        lines!(ax, weeks, mat[m, :]; color = (arm_colors[arm], 0.25), linewidth = 1)
    end
    lines!(ax, weeks, vec(mean(mat, dims = 1)); color = arm_colors[arm], linewidth = 2.6)
end
hidespines!(ax, :t, :r)
Legend(fig[1, 2], [LineElement(color = :steelblue, linewidth = 2.6),
                   LineElement(color = :tomato, linewidth = 2.6)],
       ["Vehicle", "Treatment"], framevisible = false)
fig
```
